Our model still consumes text, but instead of creating an embedding matrix from subword tokens, we render the raw, unsegmented text as images, divide it into overlapping slices, and produce representations using techniques from optical character recognition (OCR). The rest of the architecture remains unchanged.

We propose to translate from visual text representations... We demonstrate the potential of visual representations for machine translation across a range of languages, scripts, and training data sizes (Sec 4).

We introduced visually rendered text for continuous openvocabulary translation. We showed that our models, trained on seven language pairs and in two data settings, approach or match the performance of traditional text models.
